meta.title: Three-dimensional bioprinting of stem cell-derived central nervous system cells enables astrocyte growth, vasculogenesis, and enhances neural differentiation/function.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: A brain-soft PEG matrix with RGD, YIGSR and collagen IV was printed with iPSC-derived astrocytes, neural progenitors and brain endothelial-like cells. Printing supported astrocyte growth, vessel-like networks and better neural differentiation.

formulations.stiffness_note: matrix stiffness matched to human brain
formulations.review_notes: Print method inferred from the RASTRUM droplet system; confirm.
formulations.name: PEG + RGD + YIGSR + collagen IV (1.5 kPa)
formulations.composition_detail: PEG-based matrix with RGD and YIGSR peptides and 3 mg/mL collagen IV, 1.5 kPa
formulations.cell_type: astrocytes, neural progenitors, brain endothelial-like cells
formulations.key_outcome: Printed iPSC astrocytes were 82% viable at day 1 and developed typical astrocyte morphology.

evidence.quote: full‐length collagen IV at a stiffness similar to the human brain (1.5 kPa)
iPSC‐derived astrocytes were printed with good viability (82.2% ± 10.1 SD)
containing 3 mg/mL collagen IV at 10 × 106 cells/mL for iPSC‐derived BMEC‐like cells (iBMECLs), and neural progenitor cells (NPCs) and 5 × 106 cells/mL for astrocytes
